'''Yuan Yuan''' ({{lang-zh|c=原媛}}; born 11 January 1976) is a Chinese former [[Swimming (sport)|swimmer]] who competed in the [[1996 Summer Olympics]].<ref name=sref>{{cite Sports-Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/yu/yuan-yuan-1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418060602/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/yu/yuan-yuan-1.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 April 2020 |access-date=9 June 2012}}</ref>

During a routine customs check while travelling to the [[1998 World Aquatics Championships]] in [[Perth]], Australia, [[human growth hormone]] was found in her luggage, in sufficient quantities to supply the entire Chinese women's swimming team for the duration of the championships.<ref name="Mehlman2009">{{cite book|author=Maxwell J. Mehlman|title=The Price of Perfection: Individualism and Society in the Era of Biomedical Enhancement|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=upTWUqSSfckC&pg=PA126|access-date=30 July 2012|date=21 May 2009|publisher=JHU Press|isbn=978-0-8018-9263-9|pages=126–}}</ref><ref name="SMHJul28">{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/olympics/news-london-2012/chinese-olympians-subjected-to-routine-doping-20120726-22v65.html|title=Chinese Olympians subjected to routine doping|publisher=Sydney morning Herald|access-date=2012-07-30|date=2012-07-28}}</ref> Only Yuan was sanctioned for the incident, with speculation that this was connected to the nomination of [[Juan Antonio Samaranch]] by China for the [[Nobel Peace Prize]] in 1993.<ref name="Mehlman2009"/>
